featured.title: Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Shipping Routes Under Severe Pressure
featured.content: The Middle East conflict is increasingly disrupting two of the world's important maritime energy corridors. Only four commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, compared with around 125 daily transits before the conflict. Traffic through Bab el-Mandeb also fell sharply. The disruption is increasing shipping costs and adding fresh pressure to global oil and fuel markets.
featured.imageQuery: Hormuz Bab el Mandeb shipping oil tanker

articles.title: Only Four Commodity Vessels Cross Hormuz
articles.content: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen to extremely low levels. Kpler data reported by Reuters shows only four commodity vessels transited the waterway on Monday, down from ten on Sunday and far below the roughly 125 daily commercial transits recorded before the conflict. The figures exclude some vessels that may have crossed with their tracking systems switched off. The sharp reduction is increasing concern about global energy supplies.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz cargo vessels tanker

articles.title: Bab el-Mandeb Traffic Also Declines
articles.content: The disruption is not limited to Hormuz. Kpler data showed 21 commodity vessels crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Monday, compared with 28 the previous day. The waterway links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is important for shipping between Europe, Asia and the Middle East. Lower traffic is increasing pressure on shipping companies and energy markets.
articles.imageQuery: Bab el Mandeb Red Sea shipping

articles.title: Oil Moves Above $107 as Supply Risks Increase
articles.content: Brent crude rose above $107 a barrel on Tuesday as traders assessed the continuing disruption to Middle Eastern energy infrastructure and shipping. Reuters reported Brent at around $107.35, while concerns about the Saudi pipeline outage and declining tanker traffic have increased fears of a prolonged supply shock. Analysts have warned that prices could move substantially higher if disruptions continue for several weeks.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil price global market

articles.title: Saudi East-West Pipeline Remains Offline
articles.content: Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline remains offline following attacks on the country's energy infrastructure. The pipeline normally provides a route for moving Saudi crude towards the Red Sea, reducing reliance on the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reports that the disruption could place up to around 4% of global oil supply at risk if it persists.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia East West oil pipeline

articles.title: Houthi Attacks Add to Gulf Security Concerns
articles.content: Iran-aligned Houthi forces said they launched missiles and drones towards the Khamis Mushait airbase in southern Saudi Arabia. Reuters reported that the attack was presented by the Houthis as retaliation for Saudi-led operations in Yemen. The wider security situation remains fluid, and responsibility for individual incidents should not be treated as established fact unless independently confirmed.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia Houthi missile drone attack

articles.title: Dangote Refinery IPO Takes Centre Stage in Nigeria
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering is now underway in Nigeria. The company is offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 per share, targeting approximately ₦2.15 trillion, or about $1.6 billion. Reuters describes the transaction as Africa's largest IPO to date. The refinery currently operates at 700,000 barrels per day and plans to expand capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day over the next three years.

articles.title: SEC Warns Public About Dangote IPO Fraud
articles.content: Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission has issued a specific warning to prospective Dangote IPO investors. The regulator says applications and payments should only be made through officially designated and approved receiving agents, subscription channels and platforms. Investors are also warned to avoid unsolicited WhatsApp messages, social-media advertisements, emails and other offers promising guaranteed or preferential allocations.
articles.imageQuery: Nigeria SEC Abuja Securities and Exchange Commission

articles.title: Sweden Centre-Left Holds Narrow Election Lead
articles.content: Sweden's centre-left opposition remains ahead after Sunday's parliamentary election. Preliminary results put the bloc led by Magdalena Andersson at 176 seats against 173 for the right-wing bloc led by Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson. The final result is still being completed, and coalition negotiations could determine who ultimately forms the next government. Immigration, crime, the economy and support for Ukraine were among the major election issues.

articles.title: Ukraine Signals Conditional Support for Energy Ceasefire
articles.content: Ukraine has expressed conditional support for a US-backed proposal to halt attacks against energy infrastructure. President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv would need credible evidence that Russia genuinely intends to respect the arrangement. Reuters reports that no fully established formal agreement was in place, despite US President Donald Trump's statement that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy facilities.

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine Continue Energy Strikes
articles.content: Despite diplomatic efforts to reduce attacks on energy infrastructure, Russia and Ukraine have continued exchanging strikes. Reuters reports that Russia launched a major overnight drone attack affecting petrol stations and energy and port infrastructure in Ukraine, while Ukraine struck Russian oil and military-related facilities. The continued attacks are complicating attempts to establish a durable energy ceasefire.

articles.title: Global Diesel Market Faces Additional Pressure
articles.content: The global fuel market is facing pressure from disruptions in both the Middle East and Russia. Reuters reports that half of Russia's six largest diesel-producing refineries have suffered significant damage or shutdowns following Ukrainian drone attacks. Reduced Russian production, export restrictions and Middle Eastern supply disruptions are contributing to a tightening global diesel market.
articles.imageQuery: diesel fuel refinery global energy market

articles.title: AI Safety and Investment Debate Intensifies
articles.content: Artificial intelligence remains one of the world's most important technology stories. The debate is increasingly focused not only on productivity and economic growth but also on safety, regulation, infrastructure costs and whether the enormous investment in AI will generate sustainable long-term returns. Recent warnings from technology leaders have also contributed to pressure on some AI-related stocks.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence AI technology data centre

articles.title: Africa Watches Global Energy Shock Closely
articles.content: Many African economies remain vulnerable to higher international fuel and transport costs because of their dependence on imported petroleum products. Nigeria is in a different position because of its expanding domestic refining capacity. The Dangote refinery's current 700,000-barrel-per-day operation and planned expansion could become increasingly important as global shipping and energy markets remain unstable.

articles.title: Asian Markets React to Oil and Technology Risks
articles.content: Asian financial markets are responding to a combination of higher oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty and pressure on technology stocks. Investors are watching whether prolonged energy disruption will increase inflation and force central banks to maintain tighter monetary policies for longer.

morningSummary: Good afternoon. The global energy crisis is deepening as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz falls to critically low levels, with only four commodity vessels crossing on Monday. Bab el-Mandeb traffic has also declined. Brent crude has moved above $107 as the Saudi East-West pipeline remains offline following attacks. In Nigeria, the Dangote Refinery IPO is attracting major attention, while the Securities and Exchange Commission is warning investors to use only authorised subscription channels. Sweden's centre-left bloc remains narrowly ahead after Sunday's election, while Ukraine has signalled conditional support for a possible energy-infrastructure ceasefire with Russia. Meanwhile, Russian and Ukrainian attacks continue to affect energy infrastructure and the global diesel market.
bigQuestion: If the world's major energy shipping routes remain disrupted for several weeks, are we heading towards a prolonged oil-price crisis, or can governments find alternative supplies before consumers feel the full impact?
